newsitem.title: INDIA: SBC Warburg plans India broking business by yr-end.
newsitem.headline: SBC Warburg plans India broking business by yr-end.

text.p: SBC Warburg is setting up a Indian company to enter the broking business, the India chief of the Bombay representative office of Swiss Bank Corporation said on Friday.
"We are about to start a local broking firm," Euan Macdonald, India chairman of Swiss Bank Corporation said.
SBC Warburg is the investment arm of the Swiss bank.
"We are about to apply for a seat on the National Stock Exchange (NSE)," Macdonald told reporters.
The Indian broking firm will have a starting capital of $6.5 million, Macdonald said. It will be 75 percent owned by SBC Warburg and 25 percent by the private Sungrace Mafatlal Group.
Macdonald said SBC Warburg was looking forward to dematerialisation of shares to herald paperless trading.
The firm will also trade in the Indian debt market, he said.
The Indian equity research activity of SBC Warburg will become part of the proposed joint venture, he said.
The new firm is expected to begin operations before the year-end, Macdonald said.
